objects.description: HTTP template parser/holder used for transcoding HTTP paths to gRPC. Provides access to parsed path segments, HTTP verb, variable bindings, and well-known wildcard keys. Instances are constructed via the static Parse() factory. Ownership is via std::unique_ptr; copy/move semantics are not shown here. Constants for wildcard tokens are declared but defined elsewhere.
Nested type describing a {variable=...} binding within an HttpTemplate. It records the bound segment range in the path, the target protobuf field path, and whether a double-wildcard was used.
Represents one bound value for a single request message field during HTTP/REST to gRPC transcoding. Contains the protobuf field path components and the string value to insert.
Alias for std::string representing an HTTP method key (e.g., "GET", "POST") used in the PathMatcherNode result map and APIs.

Simple POD result container returned by path lookups. Holds an opaque pointer to method-specific data and a flag indicating whether the path/method was registered multiple times. Construction is trivial; no ownership semantics are defined for data (caller-managed).

Trie node used to match HTTP request paths to registered method data. Each node maintains children keyed by path parts, a mapping from HTTP method to lookup results, and a wildcard flag. Provides insertion and lookup APIs and supports cloning. Ownership: manages child nodes via unique_ptr; does not own the opaque method_data stored in results.
Value class encapsulating a sequence of path segments used when inserting paths into a PathMatcherNode. Constructed via its nested Builder; immutable after construction.
Fluent builder for PathMatcherNode::PathInfo. Accumulates path segments via AppendLiteralNode and AppendSingleParameterNode; Build() materializes a PathInfo. No ownership of external resources.
Alias for a vector of path segments used during lookup operations on the trie.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::HttpTemplate::Parse
functions.description: Parses an HTTP template string into an HttpTemplate instance. Use this to convert a template (with path segments, optional verb, and variable bindings) into a structured form for further processing (e.g., extracting segments, verb, and variables). Details of the accepted syntax follow google/api/http.proto conventions; specifics are not documented here and may need to be inferred from that specification.
requirements: ht: the HTTP template string to parse; expected to follow google/api/http.proto-style HTTP template syntax (details not provided in this header).
Return value semantics (success/failure) are not documented; callers should be prepared for parse failures (e.g., null return), though exact behavior is unknown.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::HttpTemplate::segments
functions.description: Returns the parsed path segments of the HTTP template. Intended for read-only access to the immutable list of path components extracted by Parse.
requirements: Must be called on a valid HttpTemplate instance produced by Parse or otherwise constructed.
Returned reference remains valid for the lifetime of the HttpTemplate object; do not store beyond that.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::HttpTemplate::verb
functions.description: Returns the HTTP verb suffix parsed from the template (if any). This is a read-only accessor to the verb portion captured during parsing.
requirements: Must be called on a valid HttpTemplate instance produced by Parse or otherwise constructed.
Returned reference remains valid for the lifetime of the HttpTemplate object; do not store beyond that.
Exact format/values of the verb are not specified in this header.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::HttpTemplate::Variables
functions.description: Returns a mutable reference to the collection of variable bindings extracted from the template. Each Variable describes a binding of a field path to a range of path segments, with metadata such as wildcard usage.
requirements: Must be called on a valid HttpTemplate instance produced by Parse or otherwise constructed.

Modifying the returned vector or its elements affects the owning HttpTemplate; callers must maintain internal consistency if they mutate it (e.g., segment index ranges should remain meaningful relative to segments()).

The Variable fields have the following meanings per this header: start_segment and end_segment define a half-open range over segments (end_segment may be negative to index from the end), field_path is the protobuf field path, and has_wildcard_path indicates presence of "**" in the template.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::IsReservedChar
functions.description: Returns true if c is one of the RFC 6570 reserved characters used in URI templates; false otherwise. Intended for use when deciding whether to unescape percent-encoded bytes during URL/path processing.
requirements: Input c is any 8-bit character; function assumes ASCII semantics.
No preconditions beyond providing a valid char value.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::ascii_isxdigit
functions.description: ASCII-only check for whether c is a hexadecimal digit (0-9, a-f, A-F). Not affected by locale, unlike std::isxdigit.
requirements: Input c is interpreted as ASCII; locale is intentionally ignored.
No additional preconditions; any char value is accepted.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::hex_digit_to_int
functions.description: Converts a single ASCII hex digit character to its integer value in the range [0, 15]. Assumes ASCII. If c is not a hex digit, the result is the low nibble of c’s ASCII code (unspecified for non-hex input).
requirements: Caller should ensure c is an ASCII hex digit (0-9, a-f, A-F) prior to calling (e.g., by using ascii_isxdigit).
Function assumes ASCII encoding for c.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::GetEscapedChar
functions.signature: inline int google::grpc::transcoding::GetEscapedChar(absl::string_view src, size_t i, UrlUnescapeSpec unescape_spec, bool unescape_plus, char* out)
functions.description: Helper for URL unescaping. If, at position i in src, there is a percent-encoded triplet ("%XX") that should be unescaped under unescape_spec, writes the decoded byte to *out and returns 3 (characters consumed). If unescape_plus is true and src[i] is '+', writes a space to *out and returns 1. Otherwise returns 0 and does not modify *out. Reserved characters may be left encoded depending on unescape_spec.
requirements: i must be a valid index into src (0 <= i < src.size()); the function reads src[i] unconditionally.
out must be a non-null pointer to writable memory when the function may produce an output; if return value > 0, *out is written.

Behavior depends on unescape_spec: kAllCharactersExceptReserved leaves RFC 6570 reserved characters encoded; kAllCharactersExceptSlash leaves '/' encoded; kAllCharacters decodes all percent-encoded bytes.
Assumes ASCII percent-encoding for hex digits.
Return value semantics: 0 = no unescape performed; 1 = '+' decoded to space; 3 = "%XX" decoded.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::IsUrlEscapedString
functions.signature: inline bool google::grpc::transcoding::IsUrlEscapedString(absl::string_view part, UrlUnescapeSpec unescape_spec, bool unescape_plus)
functions.description: Returns true if part contains any character sequence that would be unescaped under the given policy: either a decodable "%XX" triplet permitted by unescape_spec or (if unescape_plus is true) a '+'. Otherwise returns false.
requirements: part may be any byte sequence; interpreted as ASCII for escape detection.
No additional preconditions for parameters beyond providing valid values.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::UrlUnescapeString
functions.signature: inline std::string google::grpc::transcoding::UrlUnescapeString(absl::string_view part, UrlUnescapeSpec unescape_spec, bool unescape_plus)
functions.description: Returns a new string with part unescaped according to unescape_spec. Decodes "%XX" sequences into the corresponding byte unless restricted by the policy (e.g., reserved characters or '/'), and optionally decodes '+' to space if unescape_plus is true. Leaves other characters unchanged.
requirements: part may be any byte sequence; function assumes ASCII for hex decoding.
unescape_spec controls which decoded bytes are permitted: reserved characters (RFC 6570) or '/' may remain percent-encoded depending on the selection.
No error is thrown for malformed sequences; bytes that are not recognized as decodable under the policy are copied through unchanged.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherNode::PathInfo::Builder::Build
functions.description: Constructs and returns a PathInfo from the current Builder state. Intended to be called after appending the desired sequence of path nodes with AppendLiteralNode and/or AppendSingleParameterNode. The resulting PathInfo encapsulates the sequence of path parts to be inserted into or used with a PathMatcherNode trie.
requirements: Builder must have been initialized; it can be empty or contain previously appended nodes.
The returned PathInfo contains internal storage; it is a value and can outlive the Builder.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherNode::PathInfo::Builder::AppendLiteralNode
functions.description: Appends a literal path-part node to the builder. The part must match the exact string value of a request path segment. The documentation explicitly disallows the strings "/." and "/..".
requirements: Argument name must not be the string "/.".
Argument name must not be the string "/..".
Call can be chained; it returns the same Builder by reference.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherNode::PathInfo::Builder::AppendSingleParameterNode
functions.description: Appends a single-parameter node (wildcard for exactly one path segment) to the builder. This node matches any single request path part regardless of its string value.
requirements: Call can be chained; it returns the same Builder by reference.
No arguments; there are no documented constraints beyond using it to represent a single path segment.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherNode::PathInfo::path_info
functions.description: Returns the internal vector of path-part strings that describes the path to be inserted or matched in a PathMatcherNode trie. Provided as a const reference for read-only access.
requirements: The returned reference remains valid only while the PathInfo object remains alive; do not store the reference beyond the PathInfo lifetime.
Caller must not modify the returned container (it is const).

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherNode::PathMatcherNode
functions.description: Constructs a root PathMatcherNode with an empty method-to-result map, no children, and wildcard flag set to false.
requirements: No arguments; can be default-constructed.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherNode::~PathMatcherNode
functions.description: Destroys the PathMatcherNode and its owned resources (e.g., child nodes).
requirements: No special requirements for callers beyond ensuring no concurrent use after destruction (class is documented as Thread Compatible, not thread-safe).

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherNode::Clone
functions.description: Creates and returns a deep copy of this node and its subtrie. Useful for duplicating a matcher structure.
requirements: Callable on a valid PathMatcherNode instance.
Returned unique_ptr owns the cloned tree; caller assumes ownership.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherNode::LookupPath
functions.signature: void google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherNode::LookupPath(google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherNode::RequestPathParts::const_iterator current, google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherNode::RequestPathParts::const_iterator end, google::grpc::transcoding::HttpMethod http_method, google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherLookupResult* result) const
functions.description: Searches the trie starting at this node to find a match for the path parts in [current, end). It descends via matching children and, upon finding a terminal match for the last part, writes the associated method data and multiplicity flag into result for the specified HTTP method.
requirements: Iterators current and end must form a valid range into the same RequestPathParts container; they must be dereferenceable as the function advances.
http_method is used to select the registered method mapping; typical values are HTTP verbs (e.g., "GET", "POST"), but no specific set is enforced by the signature.
result must be a non-null pointer to a PathMatcherLookupResult to receive output.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherNode::InsertPath
functions.signature: bool google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherNode::InsertPath(const google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherNode::PathInfo& node_path_info, std::string http_method, void* method_data, bool mark_duplicates)
functions.description: Inserts a path (described by node_path_info) into this node’s subtrie. At the terminal node, associates the given http_method with method_data. Returns true if the path did not previously exist; otherwise returns false and, if mark_duplicates is true, marks the entry as having multiple registrations so lookups report multiplicity.
requirements: node_path_info must be constructed (e.g., via PathInfo::Builder) and describe the intended sequence of path parts.
http_method is the key used for method dispatch; no explicit constraints are documented.
method_data is an opaque pointer associated with the method; may be null if the caller intends to store a null payload (no constraint documented).
mark_duplicates controls duplicate handling; set to true if duplicate registrations should be flagged.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherNode::set_wildcard
functions.description: Sets whether this node represents a wildcard path "**" (matches multiple segments) in the trie.
requirements: Provide a boolean indicating the desired wildcard state. No other constraints are documented.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcher<Method>::Lookup
functions.signature:
template <class Method>
Method google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcher<Method>::Lookup(const std::string& http_method,
                                                              const std::string& path,
                                                              const std::string& query_params,
                                                              std::vector<google::grpc::transcoding::VariableBinding>* variable_bindings,
                                                              std::string* body_field_path) const
functions.description: Looks up a previously registered method by HTTP method and request path, optionally extracting variable bindings from the URL path and query string and returning the matched request body field path. Intended for request routing in an HTTP-to-RPC transcoding layer. Returns the registered Method associated with the match; returns nullptr when there is no match or on ambiguous matches. Notes: query_params should be the raw query string without the leading '?'. variable_bindings and body_field_path are optional and may be null. The implementation returns nullptr on failure, implying Method is expected to be a nullable pointer type.
requirements: http_method must exactly match the method string used during registration (including case and any appended custom verb handling).
path may include a custom verb suffix of the form ":verb" (e.g. "/v1/books:batchGet"); matching is controlled by builder configuration.
query_params should be the raw query string portion (e.g. "a=1&b=2") without the leading '?' if bindings are desired.
variable_bindings may be nullptr; if non-null, the vector will be cleared and filled with extracted bindings from both path variables and non-system query parameters.
body_field_path may be nullptr; if non-null, it will be set to the registered body field path for the matched method.
If no routes were registered (internal root_ptr_ is null) or if the lookup is ambiguous, the function returns nullptr.
Thread safety: PathMatcher is immutable and thread-safe once built; this method may be called concurrently.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherBuilder<Method>::PathMatcherBuilder
functions.description: Constructs a new PathMatcherBuilder used to register HTTP templates and associated methods before building a thread-safe PathMatcher. The builder is not thread-safe.
requirements: Do not use the builder concurrently from multiple threads.
No arguments; creates an empty trie ready for registrations.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherBuilder<Method>::Register
functions.signature:
template <class Method>
bool google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherBuilder<Method>::Register(const std::string& http_method,
                                                                     const std::string& http_template,
                                                                     const std::string& body_field_path,
                                                                     const std::unordered_set<std::string>& system_query_parameter_names,
                                                                     Method method)
functions.description: Registers a mapping from an HTTP method plus HTTP path template to the provided Method. Supports variables in the path template and records the request body field path and a set of system query parameter names to ignore when extracting bindings. Returns true on success; returns false if the path template is invalid or if duplicate insertion is disallowed by configuration.
requirements: http_template must be a valid HTTP template parsable by HttpTemplate::Parse; otherwise this returns false.
If SetFailRegistrationOnDuplicate(true) was set, attempting to register a duplicate path/method combination causes this to return false; otherwise the last registered method replaces earlier ones.
body_field_path is stored verbatim and may be empty to indicate that the entire request body maps to the request message.
system_query_parameter_names lists query parameters (e.g., "api_key") to ignore when extracting variable bindings from query parameters.
Must be called before Build().
Builder is not thread-safe; do not call concurrently.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherBuilder<Method>::SetUrlUnescapeSpec
functions.description: Configures how percent-decoding is applied to matched path variables. This setting affects only path variable extraction (not query parameters). Call before Build() to affect the resulting PathMatcher.
requirements: Call before Build() to ensure the setting is applied to the constructed PathMatcher.
This only affects path variable unescaping; it does not change query parameter unescaping.
Builder is not thread-safe; do not call concurrently.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherBuilder<Method>::SetQueryParamUnescapePlus
functions.description: When set to true, '+' in query parameter values will be unescaped to space during binding extraction (HTML 2.0/RFC1866 compatibility). Default is false.
requirements: Call before Build() to ensure the setting is applied to the constructed PathMatcher.
Affects only query parameter value decoding.
Builder is not thread-safe; do not call concurrently.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherBuilder<Method>::SetMatchUnregisteredCustomVerb
functions.description: Controls matching behavior for custom verbs in request paths (suffix after ':'). If true, attempts to match custom verbs even if they were not explicitly registered; otherwise, only registered verbs are treated as verbs.
requirements: Call before Build() to ensure the setting is applied to the constructed PathMatcher.
Builder is not thread-safe; do not call concurrently.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherBuilder<Method>::SetFailRegistrationOnDuplicate
functions.description: If set to true, subsequent Register calls will fail (return false) on duplicate path/method registrations instead of replacing the previous registration. Default is false.
requirements: Takes effect for registrations performed after this call.
Builder is not thread-safe; do not call concurrently.

functions.name: google::grpc::transcoding::PathMatcherBuilder<Method>::Build
functions.description: Finalizes registrations and returns a unique_ptr to an immutable, thread-safe PathMatcher. The builder is moved-from and should not be used after this call.
requirements: Do not use the PathMatcherBuilder instance after calling Build(); it is moved into the PathMatcher.
The returned PathMatcher may be used concurrently across threads.
Call after completing all desired configuration and Register calls.

data_types.description: A string following google/api/http.proto-style HTTP path template syntax used for HTTP-to-gRPC transcoding. Examples include literals and variables like "/v1/{name=projects/*}/topics" or paths with custom verbs like "/v1/books:batchGet". May include variable bindings {field=path} with wildcards * and **, and optional verb suffix after a colon.

A string that may contain URL percent-encoded sequences ("%XX") and optionally '+' to represent a space (HTML form-style). Used for URL path parts or query parameter values. Hex digits are ASCII; reserved characters and '/' may or may not be decoded depending on a specified unescape policy.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces URL-escaped strings tailored to exercise
# google::grpc::transcoding URL unescape helpers. It focuses on valid inputs
# across different policies: reserved chars, slash handling, plus-to-space, and
# mixtures of already-plain text with percent triplets.

# Building blocks
_HEX = "0123456789ABCDEF"
_LOWER_HEX = "0123456789abcdef"
_ASCII_PRINTABLE = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(0x20, 0x7f))
# RFC 6570 reserved characters often referenced in URI template specs
_RESERVED = ":/?#[]@!$&'()*+,;=\""  # includes slash and other reserved
_UNRESERVED = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-._~"

# Helper to percent-encode a single byte with chosen hex case
def _pct(b: int, upper: bool = True) -> str:
    hi = (b >> 4) & 0xF
    lo = b & 0xF
    hexdigits = _HEX if upper else _LOWER_HEX
    return '%' + hexdigits[hi] + hexdigits[lo]

# Construct segments that are interesting under different unescape policies
def _segment_plain(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Plain unreserved text
    length = rng.randint(1, 12)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(_UNRESERVED) for _ in range(length))

def _segment_with_plus(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix of text and plus signs which may decode to spaces depending on flag
    parts: List[str] = []
    n = rng.randint(1, 6)
    for i in range(n):
        parts.append(_segment_plain(rng))
        parts.append('+' * rng.randint(1, 3))
    parts.append(_segment_plain(rng))
    return ''.join(parts)

def _segment_with_pct_reserved(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Percent-encode reserved characters; policy may keep them encoded
    parts: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6)):
        ch = rng.choice(_RESERVED)
        upper = rng.choice([True, False])
        parts.append(_pct(ord(ch), upper))
        # sprinkle plain
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(_segment_plain(rng))
    return ''.join(parts) or _pct(ord('~'))

def _segment_with_pct_unreserved(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Percent-encoded unreserved characters should always decode
    parts: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 8)):
        ch = rng.choice(_UNRESERVED)
        upper = rng.choice([True, False])
        parts.append(_pct(ord(ch), upper))
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            parts.append(rng.choice(['', _segment_plain(rng)]))
    return ''.join(parts)

def _segment_with_slash_encoded(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Encode '/' specifically to exercise kAllCharactersExceptSlash vs others
    reps = rng.randint(1, 5)
    parts: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(reps):
        parts.append(_segment_plain(rng))
        parts.append(rng.choice(['%2F', '%2f']))
    parts.append(_segment_plain(rng))
    return ''.join(parts)

def _mixed_segment(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Combine multiple behaviors in one part
    builders = [
        _segment_plain,
        _segment_with_plus,
        _segment_with_pct_reserved,
        _segment_with_pct_unreserved,
        _segment_with_slash_encoded,
    ]
    parts: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4)):
        parts.append(rng.choice(builders)(rng))
    # Keep part modest
    s = ''.join(parts)
    if len(s) > 256:
        s = s[:256]
    return s

def _make_query_string(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create realistic query string with a variety of encodings and plus usage
    kv_count = rng.randint(1, 6)
    keys = ['key', 'q', 'page', 'filter', 'api_key', 'token', 'x']
    seg_fns = [
        _segment_plain,
        _segment_with_plus,
        _segment_with_pct_unreserved,
        _segment_with_pct_reserved,
        _segment_with_slash_encoded,
        _mixed_segment,
    ]
    pairs = []
    for _ in range(kv_count):
        k = rng.choice(keys) + (str(rng.randint(0, 9)) if rng.random() < 0.4 else '')
        v = rng.choice(seg_fns)(rng)
        pairs.append(f"{k}={v}")
    return '&'.join(pairs)

def _make_path_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create a path-like string composed of segments; the fuzz stubs may use it
    seg_count = rng.randint(1, 8)
    seg_fns = [
        _segment_plain,
        _segment_with_pct_unreserved,
        _segment_with_pct_reserved,
        _segment_with_slash_encoded,  # will stay within a single segment since '/' is encoded
        _segment_with_plus,
        _mixed_segment,
    ]
    segments = [rng.choice(seg_fns)(rng) for _ in range(seg_count)]
    s = '/'.join(segments)
    # Optionally append a custom verb suffix to simulate paths that include ':'
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        verb = rng.choice(['batchGet', 'search', 'upload'])
        s += ':' + verb
    return s

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose one of several composition modes to align with various stub needs
    mode = rng.randint(0, 5)
    if mode == 0:
        # Single part focusing on unreserved percent triplets
        part = _segment_with_pct_unreserved(rng)
    elif mode == 1:
        # Single part focusing on reserved encodings
        part = _segment_with_pct_reserved(rng)
    elif mode == 2:
        # Plus handling emphasis
        part = _segment_with_plus(rng)
    elif mode == 3:
        # Slash encoded emphasis
        part = _segment_with_slash_encoded(rng)
    elif mode == 4:
        # Path-like string with multiple segments and optional custom verb
        part = _make_path_like(rng)
    else:
        # Query-string like payload to feed into IsUrlEscapedString/UrlUnescapeString
        part = _make_query_string(rng)

    # Ensure non-empty and within size limits
    if not part:
        part = '%41'  # 'A'

    b = part.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
    return b
